summary: Filed from the Flow-rename session: npm start died immediately while npm run test:desktop was running. Verified at the time that the suite takes its own free port (60525, 61661) and a per-test CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA, and that nothing was listening on 3000 - so neither port nor profile collided. main.js sets userData at 258 BEFORE requestSingleInstanceLock at 291, which should already isolate the lock, so the mechanism is NOT understood and the card opens at research. Second suspect with an identical symptom: server.js exits non-zero on EADDRINUSE and main.js makes that fatal. Repro must name which fires (silent quit = lock, app.log fatal = port) before any guard ships.

todo -> doing (validating). Premise DISPROVEN by three one-variable probes on Electron 41.1.1/Win11 with the dev app running: a test-profile instance (CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA + own CUBRIC_PORT) lived 25s beside it, so requestSingleInstanceLock IS scoped by userData and no test Electron can take the user lock; a plain dev-profile launch reproduced the symptom exactly (exit 0 at 2282ms, splash ERR_FAILED, no EADDRINUSE and no app.log fatal = lock signature, not port); the same launch with ONLY the profile changed lived 20s. Root = ordinary single-instance lock firing because another default-profile instance was already open; the suite was coincident, not causal. The proposed CUBRIC_E2E guard must NOT ship - its only reachable effect is letting a spec that forgot CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA boot against the users real profile, trading a loud quit for silent corruption. Owed: full test:desktop + concurrent npm start confirmation, deferred while a live model smoke test held the machine.
